story.head: The Rangers hunt better looks than the Flames
paras: The Flames (8-9-1) beat Philadelphia 4-3 in overtime on Sunday, and the Rangers have won three straight. Going in, the Rangers are third in the Metropolitan (tied for 12th in the NHL) and the Flames fifth in the Pacific (tied for 21st).

The Rangers lean on their stars as much as almost anyone (2nd lowest), forecheck as hard as almost anyone (2nd) and get a lot of their shots blocked (32nd). The Flames play some of the league’s fastest games (2nd) and take more penalties than they draw (30th). They also take a lot of low-quality shots (32nd), so the Rangers wait for good looks, but them settle for hopeful ones. The Rangers are likely to get in the way of a lot of the Flames’ shots.

Adam Fox (2 G / 20 A / 22 P in 18 GP) leads the Rangers in scoring. Alexis Lafrenière (9 G / 9 A / 18 P in 18 GP) has a team-high nine goals, with five goals in six games against Calgary since 2023-24. For the Flames, Joel Farabee (7 G / 10 A / 17 P in 18 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Matt Coronato (4 G / 11 A / 15 P in 18 GP) is next in line.
Dylan Garand (6-6-1 / .906 SV% in 11 GS) is in line to start for the Rangers. Dustin Wolf (3-5-1 / .869 SV% in 9 GS) has had a rough start to the season for Calgary, but will likely start.
At home, Ryan Huska likes to send Farabee, Backlund and Coronato out against the other team’s top line, so watch for them against Lafrenière, Zibanejad and Perreault.
